text:
Predicates:
BredBack(x) ::: x is bred-back.
DomesticAnimal(x) ::: x is a domestic animal.
SelectiveBreeding(x) ::: x is a form of artificial selection by deliberate selective breeding.
Resemble(x, y) ::: x resembles y.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Extinct(x) ::: x is extinct.
Premises:
∀x (BredBack(x) → (SelectiveBreeding(x) ∧ DomesticAnimal(x))) ::: Breeding back is a form of artificial selection by the deliberate selective breeding of domestic animals.
BredBack(heckCattle) ∧ Resemble(heckCattle, aurochs) ∧ Resemble(aurochs, extinctAnimal) ::: Heck cattle were bred-back in the 1920s to resemble the aurochs. Some animals to be bred-back resemble animals that are extinct.
Animal(heckCattle) ::: Heck cattle are animals.
Animal(aurochs) ::: Aurochs are animals.
Conclusion:
∃x (HeckCattle(x) ∧ BredBack(x)) ::: Some Heck cattle are artificially selected.
